What happens to my Google Photos when I die?

Short answer: Google Photos lives inside your Google Account, so it follows Google's rules. Add Photos to Inactive Account Manager and your chosen contacts can download it after the inactivity period. Without a plan, family must use Google's deceased-user data request, which isn't guaranteed. Shared albums and Takeout backups made now are the safest route.

Key facts

  • Covered by Inactive Account Manager
  • No plan: deceased-user data request, reviewed case by case
  • Inactive accounts can be deleted after 2 years
  • Back up now with Google Takeout

How do I prepare my Google Photos account?

  1. Add Google Photos to the data shared through Inactive Account Manager.
  2. Use Google Photos partner sharing or shared albums with family now.
  3. Export a full copy periodically with Google Takeout and store it offline.
  4. Write down where the backups are in your digital estate plan.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • Death certificate
  • Your ID and the account address
  • Possibly further legal documents for a data request

How long does it take?

Contacts get a download link only after the inactivity period you chose. Data requests have no published timeframe.

What can't be recovered?

  • Photos only stored in an account deleted for inactivity
  • Contents of an account already closed at family's request

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Google Photos when I die?

Google Photos lives inside your Google Account, so it follows Google's rules. Add Photos to Inactive Account Manager and your chosen contacts can download it after the inactivity period. Without a plan, family must use Google's deceased-user data request, which isn't guaranteed. Shared albums and Takeout backups made now are the safest route.

Will my Google Photos be deleted when I die?

They can be deleted if the account stays inactive for 2 years, so set up Inactive Account Manager and a Takeout backup.

Can I give someone my photos automatically?

Yes. Inactive Account Manager can share your Google Photos data with up to 10 contacts.

How do I back up my Google Photos?

Use Google Takeout and select Google Photos; store the archive offline and in a second location.

Can family request photos without a plan?

They can ask through Google's deceased-user form, but Google decides each request after review.
